record.paper_title: Mathematical open problems in Projected Entangled Pair States
record.original_question: Give an explicit and computable function f(D), preferably polynomial in the PEPS bond dimension D, that upper-bounds the injectivity index of every normal projected entangled pair state with bond dimension D.

evidence.quote: As opposed to the 1D case, the only known result ... is the existence of a function of the bond dimension f(D) that bounds i(A) for every PEPS with bond dimension D. Unfortunately, in principle such function could be uncomputable.
Question 5 Give an explicit (computable and if possible polynomial) function f(D) which is an upper bound for the injectivity index of a normal PEPS.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Consider a translation-invariant Projected Entangled Pair State (PEPS) on the two-dimensional square lattice defined by a single tensor

  A : (C^D)^{⊗4} → C^d,

where D is the bond dimension and d is the physical dimension. For any finite simply connected region R of the lattice, contracting copies of A on the sites of R with open physical indices and with open virtual indices on the boundary ∂R yields a linear map

  Γ_R : (C^D)^{⊗|∂R|} → (C^d)^{⊗|R|}.

The PEPS tensor A is said to be injective on R if Γ_R is injective. The injectivity index i(A) is the smallest integer L such that Γ_R is injective for every square block region R of side length at least L. The PEPS is called normal if some such finite L exists, i.e. i(A) < ∞.

It is known that there exists a function f : N → N such that i(A) ≤ f(D) for every normal PEPS tensor A with bond dimension D, but the only proofs of existence available do not yield a computable f.

Problem. Exhibit an explicit, computable function f : N → N — and ideally a polynomial one — such that for every normal PEPS tensor A with bond dimension D one has

  i(A) ≤ f(D).
artifact.status_search_result: A search of recent literature on PEPS injectivity, normal PEPS, and quantum Wielandt-type inequalities in 2D shows that, while the 1D analogue (matrix product states) admits an O(D^2 log D)-type bound via the quantum Wielandt inequality, no explicit computable upper bound on the injectivity index of a normal 2D PEPS in terms of the bond dimension D appears to have been established. Recent work (e.g. on computational complexity of injective PEPS and on generalizations of the injectivity condition) does not provide such a function. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Computational complexity of injective projected entangled pair states
status_evidence.snippet: Studies complexity of injective PEPS but does not establish a computable upper bound on the injectivity index in terms of bond dimension.
status_evidence.claim: Recent (2025) work on injective PEPS focuses on complexity rather than producing an explicit computable bound f(D) on the injectivity index.

status_evidence.title: A generalization of the injectivity condition for Projected Entangled Pair States
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses injectivity and normal PEPS and the relation between bond dimensions.
status_evidence.claim: Generalizations of injectivity have been studied, but no explicit computable bound on i(A) in terms of D has been derived.
